title: Built-In Tag Helpers
description: Use ASP.NET Core's built-in tag helpers for forms, links, inputs, caching, and asset management.

data.text: ASP.NET Core ships with a rich set of built-in tag helpers that remove repetitive HTML and keep your views correct as your routes and models change. In this lesson you will learn the most important ones: Form, Anchor, Input, Select, Label, and Cache.

terms.definition: Generates the form action attribute and adds an antiforgery token automatically.
Builds an href from controller, action, and route values.
Binds an <input> element to a model property using asp-for.
Populates an HTML <select> from a data source using asp-items.
Caches rendered content for a configurable duration to improve performance.

data.text: Form Tag Helper
The Form Tag Helper targets the `<form>` element. It generates the `action` attribute from your route configuration and, by default, adds a hidden antiforgery token to protect against CSRF attacks.

data.title: Form Tag Helper with controller and action attributes
data.content: The form's action is generated from the route configuration.

data.text: Key form attributes:

rows: Targets a specific controller for the form action.
Targets a specific action method for the form action.
Adds a route value (e.g. asp-route-id adds the id segment).
Generates a hidden antiforgery token. Enabled by default for POST forms.

data.title: CSRF protection
data.text: Always validate the antiforgery token on the server. Decorate your HTTP POST action with [ValidateAntiForgeryToken].

data.title: Enforcing antiforgery validation on the server
data.content: Decorate the POST action to validate the antiforgery token.

data.text: Anchor Tag Helper
The Anchor Tag Helper enhances `<a>` elements by generating the `href` from routing data. It prevents broken links when routes change and supports route parameters, areas, and fragments.

data.content: Linking to a details page with an id route value.

data.text: Input, Label, and Select Tag Helpers
These tag helpers bind HTML form controls to model properties. The `asp-for` attribute is the key — it accepts a lambda expression (or a string in Razor Pages) that points to a model property.
Label Tag Helper
Sets the `for` attribute on a `<label>` so clicking it focuses the associated input:

data.title: Label Tag Helper bound to a model property
data.content: The label's for attribute is set automatically.

data.text: Rendered output:

data.title: Generated label and input HTML
data.content: Both elements now share the same id and name.
data.code:
<label for="Product_Name">Name</label>
<input type="text" id="Product_Name" name="Product.Name" value="" class="form-control" />

data.text: Input Tag Helper
The Input Tag Helper sets `type`, `id`, `name`, and `value` based on the model property's .NET type:

data.title: Input Tag Helper bound to different property types
data.content: ASP.NET Core chooses the correct input type automatically.
data.code:
<input asp-for="Product.Name" class="form-control" />
<input asp-for="Product.Price" class="form-control" />
<input asp-for="Product.InStock" class="form-check-input" />
<input asp-for="Product.Created" class="form-control" />

data.text: Select Tag Helper
The Select Tag Helper populates a `<select>` element from a data source. Use `asp-for` for the bound property and `asp-items` for the option list:

data.title: Select Tag Helper populated from ViewBag
data.content: Populating a dropdown using a SelectList in the controller.

data.title: Automatic selection
data.text: If the model's bound property already has a value, the Select Tag Helper automatically marks the matching option as selected.
Cache Tag Helper

The Cache Tag Helper caches the rendered content of its body. Use it for fragments that are expensive to compute but do not need to be fresh on every request — for example, a navigation menu or a footer.

data.title: Cache Tag Helper with a sliding expiration
data.content: Cache the content for 60 seconds after the last request.

rows: Relative time after which the cache entry expires.
Absolute DateTime at which the cache entry expires.
Resets the expiration timer on each request.
Creates separate cache entries per value of the given key.
Creates separate cache entries per query string key.
Creates separate cache entries per cookie value.

data.title: Don't cache user-specific data
data.text: The Cache Tag Helper stores content in a shared cache. Never cache data that is specific to the logged-in user unless you vary by that user's identity.
JavaScript and CSS Tag Helpers
The JavaScript and CSS Tag Helpers manage which scripts and stylesheets are included in a view. They support wildcard patterns, CDN fallback, and cache-busting.

data.title: JavaScript Tag Helper with CDN fallback
data.content: Load jQuery from a CDN with a local fallback.

data.title: CSS Tag Helper with cache busting
data.content: Link a stylesheet with a version query string for cache busting.

data.text: The `asp-append-version` attribute adds a checksum query string (e.g. `?v=abc123`) to the URL. When the file changes, the checksum changes and the browser downloads the new version.
Exercise: Build a Product Create Form

data.title: Exercise: Build a Create form with built-in tag helpers
data.description: Use the Form, Label, Input, Select, and Anchor Tag Helpers to build a complete create form.
steps: Create a Product model with Name (string), Price (decimal), CategoryId (int), and InStock (bool).
Add a Create GET action that populates a SelectList for CategoryId in ViewBag.
Add a Create POST action with [ValidateAntiForgeryToken] that saves the product.
In the view, use the Form Tag Helper with asp-controller and asp-action.
Use the Label and Input Tag Helpers for Name, Price, and InStock.
Use the Select Tag Helper with asp-items for CategoryId.
Add an Anchor Tag Helper that links back to the Index page.
Run the app and confirm the form submits and redirects correctly.
data.expectedOutcome: A fully functional create form where every element uses the appropriate built-in tag helper, and the generated HTML is clean and correct.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: The Form Tag Helper generates the action URL and adds an antiforgery token.
The Anchor Tag Helper keeps links correct as your routes change.
asp-for binds HTML controls to model properties, setting id, name, type, and value automatically.
The Select Tag Helper uses asp-items with a SelectList to render options.
The Cache Tag Helper improves performance by caching rendered fragments.
asp-append-version adds a checksum for cache busting on static assets.
data.takeaway: Built-in tag helpers cover 90% of everyday view scenarios. When you need behavior they do not provide, it is time to write a custom tag helper — which is exactly what the next lesson covers.
